children: shares surged 25% in extended trading Wednesday after the backup-power company disclosed a long-term supply agreement with Amazon
that calls for $2.4 billion of initial generator deliveries in 2027 and 2028.
The agreement could eventually generate as much as $8 billion in payments to Generac
and its global affiliates, according to a regulatory filing. The generators will provide backup power for Amazon data centers.

The deal gives Generac significant exposure to the rapid expansion of data-center infrastructure as Amazon and other technology companies invest heavily in computing capacity for artificial intelligence and cloud services. Backup generators help data centers continue operating during power failures or disruptions to the electrical grid.
As part of the transaction, Generac issued an Amazon subsidiary a warrant to purchase as many as 1.69 million Generac shares at an exercise price of $200.9266 each.

About 307,954 shares covered by the warrant vested immediately. The remainder will vest in stages as Generac receives payments connected with Amazon’s generator purchases, up to the $8 billion threshold.
The warrant can be exercised through Sept. 16, 2033, subject to its vesting terms and other conditions. Amazon may exercise it by paying cash or through a cashless transaction.
The arrangement gives Amazon a potential equity stake in Generac while tying most of that opportunity to the volume of business it sends to the manufacturer.

Generac is best known for residential standby generators, a business whose demand can fluctuate with severe weather, power outages and housing-market conditions. The Amazon agreement adds a large commercial customer and provides greater visibility into future sales.

The initial $2.4 billion delivery commitment over two years represents a substantial order for Generac. More importantly, the possibility of payments reaching $8 billion suggests the relationship could extend well beyond the first phase if Amazon continues expanding its data-center network.
Investors’ enthusiastic response reflects both the size of the initial deliveries and the potential for Generac to become a major supplier to the power-hungry data-center industry.

title: Generac surges on $2.4B Amazon data-center deal
